data.title: Multibagger stock: SG Mart surges 13% to record high on fundraise buzz
data.description:
SG Mart share price today: Shares of SG Mart extended their winning streak for a second consecutive session on Monday, hitting an all-time high despite weakness in the market. The stock opened 4.5 per cent higher at ₹1,150 and extended its gains to hit an intraday high of ₹1,238.70, rising 13 per cent.
 
The buying interest in the stock was supported by an announcement that the company may consider a fund-raising proposal.
 
As of 9:50 AM, SG Mart shares were trading 12.3 per cent higher at ₹1,231, retaining most of their intraday gains.
 
The stock was among the most actively traded equities by value. According to exchange data, around two million shares changed hands, with a total turnover of ₹233.35 crore.
 
 
With Monday's rally, the stock has gained 21 per cent over two consecutive trading sessions.
 
SG Mart fundraise news 
 
SG Mart, a B2B building materials and steel processing company, informed the exchanges that its board of directors will meet on November 26 to consider a proposal to raise funds. 
ALSO READ: Stock Market LIVE: Sensex down 500 points, Nifty near 25,600; PSU bank, metal indices down 2%
 
The funds will be raised by way of issue of one or more instruments, including equity shares/ convertible securities either by way of Preferential Issue/ Rights Issue/ QIP/ or any other method or combination thereof as may be permitted.
 
SG Mart stock performance 
 
SG Mart shares have significantly outperformed the markets in 2026 so far. According to exchange data, the stock has rallied 54 per cent in the past month, compared with a 13 per cent gain in the benchmark Nifty 50. On a Y-T-D basis, the stock has surged 219 per cent, while the Nifty 50 has declined around 2 per cent. The stock has soared 250 per cent over the past year.
 
SG Mart stock: Analyst view
 
Vipin Kumar, AVP, equity research (derivatives & technical analyst), Globe Capital Market, said that SG Mart stock has been consistently forming higher highs and higher lows since its listing in the secondary market, reflecting strong price performance and a robust chart structure. Considering the current technical setup, we recommend traders wait for a corrective dip before initiating fresh long positions. 
 
"A decline towards ₹1,050 would offer a favourable buying opportunity from a medium-term perspective," he said.

data.title: Weekly policy watch: Nepal PM Shah's India visit, PMI flash data in focus
data.description:
India’s diplomatic and economic calendar this week will focus on Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah’s visit to New Delhi, along with fresh readings on manufacturing and services activity.
 

Nepal PM Balendra Shah to hold talks with Modi

 
Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah is scheduled to hold delegation-level talks with Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Monday. The two leaders are expected to review the full range of India-Nepal relations and exchange views on regional and international issues of mutual interest, the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said.
 
Shah arrived in India on Sunday for a two-day state visit from November 22 to 23 at PM Modi’s invitation. This is his first visit to India since taking office in March 2026 and his first bilateral visit abroad as Nepal’s prime minister.
 
 
External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar met Shah in New Delhi on Sunday and said India values its special friendship with Nepal. In a post on X, Jaishankar shared a photograph of the meeting and said he looked forward to Shah’s engagements with PM Modi on Monday.
 

PMI Flash data on November 23

 
The HSBC Manufacturing and Services PMI Flash data for November will be released on November 23.
 
India’s manufacturing activity moderated in October, with the HSBC India Manufacturing PMI falling to 54.7 from 55.1 in September. Growth in output and new orders slowed during the month. However, strong overseas demand pushed new export orders to a six-month high, while selling price inflation fell to its lowest level in nearly four years.
 
The services sector, meanwhile, expanded at its fastest pace in four months in October, supported by stronger domestic demand and new business orders. The HSBC India Services PMI rose to 55.8 in October from 55.2 in September, marking the strongest expansion since June.
 
The reading remained above the 50 mark, which separates expansion from contraction, as well as its long-term average. New business increased at its fastest pace in four months, with companies citing favourable demand, new client acquisitions and successful advertising campaigns.
 

Deposit growth data on November 27

 
The RBI will release bank deposit growth data on November 27, offering an update on the pace at which banks are attracting deposits.
 
Deposit growth in India rose to 16.9 per cent in the week ended October 30 from 16.7 per cent two weeks earlier.
 
Deposit growth averaged 14.72 per cent between 1998 and 2026. It reached a record high of 29.3 per cent in January 2008 and a low of 2.7 per cent in December 2017.
 

Forex reserves data on November 27

 
The RBI will release foreign exchange reserves data for the week ended November 20 on November 27.
 
India’s forex reserves fell by $14.21 billion to $705.34 billion in the week ended November 13, according to the latest RBI data. Reserves had stood at $719.55 billion in the previous week ended November 6.
 
Foreign currency assets (FCAs), the largest component of the reserves, declined by $7.9 billion to $583.45 billion during the reported week.

data.title: Eicher Motors hits all-time high; here's why stock rallied 17% in one month
data.description:
Eicher Motors share price movement

 
Share price of Eicher Motors, the maker of Royal Enfield (RE) motorcycles, hit an all-time high of ₹8,266.90, gaining 2 per cent on the National Stock Exchange (NSE) in Monday’s intraday deals. This occurred as the management expressed confidence in sustaining growth through new launches, premiumisation and capacity expansion to 2 million units by the second quarter of the financial year 2027-28 (Q2FY28).
 
The stock price of the two-wheeler company surpassed its previous high of ₹8,232.80 touched on February 27, 2026. In the past month, it outperformed the market and rallied 17 per cent. In comparison, the Nifty 50 was up 13.7 during the same period. 
 
 
At 09:40 AM, Eicher Motors was up 0.50 per cent at ₹8,152.50, compared to a 0.54 per cent decline in the Nifty 50 and a 0.29 per cent drop in the Nifty Auto index.  CHECK Stock Market LIVE Updates 

Eicher Motors – Healthy management commentary

 
Eicher Motors achieved its highest-ever monthly sales in September and October, and continued that trend through the festive period, driven by growth across the company’s portfolio, the management said in its Q2FY27 earnings conference call.
 
Eicher Motors expanded its electric vehicle (EV) footprint to Europe and the UK with the launch of Flying Flea C6. VE Commercial Vehicles (VECV) also achieved its best-ever second quarter sales, delivering robust multi segment growth. 
 
Collectively, this performance drove Eicher to a record first-half, and the management said they remain poised to sustain this trajectory in the upcoming quarters. Given the market situation with positive customer sentiment and a full and growing booking pipeline, the management said the company is scaling up production and improving inventory and channel readiness to cater to the demand. Check - TOP GAINERS NSE | TOP LOSERS NSE 

Brokerages view on Eicher Motors

 
Royal Enfield continues to witness a healthy demand, with volume growth currently constrained more by supply than demand. Accelerating capacity expansion, a robust product pipeline and sustained premiumisation provide strong visibility for medium-term volume growth over FY28–30, said analysts at Systematix Institutional Equities in the result update.
 
Meanwhile, VECV continues to demonstrate strong execution, improving operating leverage and broad-based demand momentum. A robust booking pipeline, lean dealer inventory and rising production capacity position Royal Enfield for stronger wholesale growth over the coming quarters, the brokerage firm said, as it remains positive on Eicher Motors’ medium-term growth prospects, supported by capacity-led volume expansion, premiumisation and improving earnings contribution from VECV. Analysts retained a 'Buy' rating on Eicher Motors with a target price of ₹8,910 (earlier ₹8,100).
 
With demand visibility, manufacturing expansion, premiumisation, and international opportunities supporting its medium- to long-term business prospects along with a strong growth outlook for the VECV arm, analysts at ICICI Securities maintain a 'Buy' rating on the stock. Analysts value Eicher Motors at ₹9,500 (SOTP basis, 35x PE to RE business & 25x PE to VECV arm on average of FY28-29E EPS).
 
Royal Enfield remains well-positioned to benefit from the structural premiumisation of the Indian 2W industry. In Q2FY27, 2W volumes continued with healthy performance, with sales at 6.43 million units, up 15 per cent year-on-year (YoY). The company currently commands approximately 83 per cent market share in the domestic middleweight segment (250cc-750cc), while its overall motorcycle market share remains at just 9 per cent.
 
Sustained booking growth of 21 per cent, low dealer inventory & waiting periods of <= 2 months (certain models) indicate that underlying demand remains stronger than current supply. Furthermore, ongoing product interventions, and upcoming launches should support volume growth & strengthen Royal Enfield's positioning going forward, the brokerage firm said. 
Analysts at JM Financial Institutional Securities said in the auto sector update said the demand momentum remained healthy in October 2026 with domestic 2W ICE and passenger vehicle volumes growing 12 per cent and 12.5 per cent year-on-year (YoY), respectively, despite a high base (October 2025 benefited from Diwali and post-GST 2.0 demand), With Dhanteras/Diwali falling in early November this year, November 2026 volumes should also benefit from festive demand. While demand momentum is expected to remain healthy for H2FY27, growth rates would taper off given the higher base. On the other hand, input cost volatility remains, which could limit margin expansion, at least in the near term, the brokerage firm said.  In this scenario, analysts said they would prefer companies that have a healthy launch pipeline and better earnings visibility.

data.title: Bisleri disputes FSSAI findings after prosecution sanction over water
data.description:
Bisleri International Pvt Ltd on Monday claimed its packaged drinking water was safe for consumption after the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) sanctioned prosecution against the company over a sample found non-compliant with prescribed safety standards.
 
In a statement, the company said the matter concerned a batch produced in September 2025 at its Goa manufacturing facility. It disputed the laboratory findings and said subsequent independent testing found bromate levels within the prescribed limit.
 
The FSSAI action followed the detection of bromate beyond the permissible limit in a sample of Bisleri's packaged drinking water. The referral laboratory also declared the sample unsafe after detecting polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), according to the regulator.
 

Bisleri disputes laboratory findings

According to the company's statement, FSSAI collected six samples from its Goa facility on September 30, 2025. Initial testing found that five samples met the applicable standards, while the sixth recorded bromate levels of 12 micrograms per litre, against the prescribed limit of 10 micrograms per litre.
 
Bisleri appealed against the findings on November 22, 2025, following which FSSAI sent the sample to a referral laboratory for retesting.
 
The referral laboratory found bromate levels within the prescribed limit but separately detected polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) in the sample, the company claimed in its statement.
 
Bisleri said it subsequently arranged for the same sample to be tested independently at an FSSAI-approved laboratory. The test also found bromate levels within the prescribed limit, according to the company.

Bisleri claims it received no further communication

Bisleri submitted the independent laboratory results to FSSAI's Western Regional Office through a formal letter dated February 2, 2026.
 
"We received no further communication from FSSAI after that submission and understood the matter to be closed," the company said.
 
It also claimed it had not received any notice by email or in hard copy and had been unable to locate the reported notice on FSSAI's website.

Bisleri cites quality checks

The company said it conducts more than 90 quality tests across its 10-step manufacturing process.
 
"We will continue to cooperate with FSSAI to address the matter through the appropriate regulatory process," Bisleri said.

data.title: Tata Steel divests tubes biz: Will it unlock value? What analysts say
data.description:
Tata Steel share price: Tata group company Tata Steel has announced a strategic divestment plan, which will help unlock value for the steel major, analysts believe. 
 
While Tata Steel shares slumped almost 6 per cent following the deal announcement on Monday, brokerages largely retained their bullish views on the counter, with both Emkay and JM Financial assigning 'BUY' calls. On Monday, Tata Steel stock was down 6.04 per cent at ₹167.
 
As part of the agreement, Tata Steel has approved divestment of its tubes business and its entire equity stake in Tata Steel Colors (formerly Tata BlueScope Steel) to APL Apollo for aggregate consideration of up to ₹28000 crore (equivalent to approximately ₹22/share). 
 
 
The Tubes Business will be transferred for cash consideration of up to ₹11700 crore, while the entire 100 per cent stake in Tata Steel Colors will be sold for ₹16300 crore in cash. Both transactions are inter-conditional and are expected to close
simultaneously, subject to regulatory approvals and customary conditions, by March 31, 2028.
 
Furthermore, earlier on Monday, the company said it will also pick a majority stake in the company by acquiring the entire promoter stake of 26.6 per cent in APL Apollo, an MOU with SG Tech Engineering Private Ltd, a company associated with the Promoter Group of APL Apollo, to set up exclusive contract manufacturing facilities of 5 MTPA of Colour Coated products.
 
What analysts say on Tata Steel
Analysts believe the deal announced could lead to significant value unlocking of through sale of downstream business, but also marks a pivot away from the earlier planned expansion of tubes capacity, along with doubling the Colors business.
 
"We view the transactions positively as a significant value-unlocking exercise and an important step towards downstream portfolio rationalisation," said JM Financial analysts. 
 
The aggregate consideration of up to ₹28000 crore provides substantial cash realisation and financial flexibility, equivalent to approximately 31 per cent of Tata Steel’s September 2026 consolidated net debt of ₹91423 crore. 
 
The monetisation, said JM Financial, allows Tata Steel to unlock capital from downstream businesses and potentially redeploy it towards core steelmaking operations, capacity expansion and balance-sheet strengthening. 
 
Meanwhile, Emkay Global said that while it views the transaction as a significant strategic reset for Tata Steel, it is unsure if is an unambiguously positive portfolio-rationalization exercise. 
 
The consideration offers meaningful capital unlocking (~80 per cent of FY26 EBITDA and 31 per cent of 2Q net debt-to-EBITDA), but the divestment of businesses generating ₹16100 crore in revenue, along with combined net worth of Rs43bn, needs to be assessed against the earnings and growth potential being relinquished. 
 
Loss of downstream conversion economics and strategic optionality also warrants attention, especially without a disclosed long-term supply arrangement with APL Apollo, it noted. Emkay has a 'BUY' rating and a target price of ₹210 on the stock.
 
JM also noted the loss of earnings from the divested businesses, but added that transactions could improve capital efficiency, sharpen strategic focus and strengthen Tata Steel’s financial flexibility," it added. This brokerage has a 'BUY' call with a target of ₹240.

data.title: Gold, Copper, Zinc, Aluminium: Morgan Stanley's outlook on key metals
data.description:
Prices of metals such as copper, zinc, aluminium, gold and silver have been on a downtrend since the last few trading sessions in India and globally, as concerns regarding rising inflation higher yields, possibility of 'higher for longer' interest rates in the United States (US) and a pullback in artificial intelligence (AI)- related spending cast a shadow.
 
The Nifty Metal index slid over 2 per cent in trade on Monday, with stocks such as Tata Steel, Hindustan Copper, Sail, NMDC, National Aluminium slipping up to 5.5 per cent in intraday deals. APL Apollo Tubes, though news-driven, was the top loser that skidded over 13 per cent in intraday deals. 
ALSO READ: APL Apollo tanks 14%, Tata Steel 5% on ₹28K-cr deal: What it means for cos
 
 
Rate cuts through 2024/2025, the AI theme and focus on strategic minerals had boosted investor engagement in metals, according to analysts at Morgan Stanley, with positioning back at 2021/22 levels. With interest rates rising again though, metals are struggling as a non-yielding asset with exposure to rate-sensitive construction and autos markets.
 
The weakness in the AI theme is not helping, particularly for copper, Morgan Stanley said in a November 18 report, which had held up relative to other AI-exposed assets, while a stronger US dollar (USD) also hurts.
 
Here's how Morgan Stanley sees prices of metals play out in the next few months.
 
Gold: Gold's long-term drivers remain intact. Physical demand is holding up well, with China's PBOC adding 26 tonnes in October and central bank buying on track to surpass 2025 levels, while exchange traded funds (ETFs) seeing very modest gold sales so far despite falling prices. This suggests support for real assets driven by concerns over government debt and fiscal sustainability. 
 
If oil prices move lower more decisively and/or the market gets to the point where it believes the US Fed has finished hiking, gold prices could move higher, while a stagflation scenario with softer growth and more stubborn inflation could also be supportive. Timing remains challenging though, and the systematic positioning moves and sensitivity to technical levels could keep gold volatility high in the short-term. 
ALSO READ: Copper falls to near five-month low as firm dollar, AI concerns weigh
 
Copper: The cautious view on copper by end-2027 has played out quicker-than-expected with a combination of factors driving the weakness. Negative macro pressure from rising interest rates and stronger USD was already building for commodities as a whole, while the broad-based AI selloff has brought additional weakness.
 
Copper has seen a strong correlation with the "Mag7" stocks this year, implying some of its elevated positioning was related to the AI build-out. Our thesis of copper deficit into next year remains unchanged, and we would remain buyers if there is an overshoot (MSe $13,675/t for LME 2027 average, $12,800/t (Q4 2027).
 
With the need for more projects to be developed to avoid large future deficits, copper is expected to broadly stay above incentive price (MSe $10,700/t real 2026$, $12,400/t nominal 2033), but it's difficult to call exactly when dip buying will emerge, and we can of course have volatility around that level with changes in AI sentiment and US tariff policy.  
 
 
Aluminium: Aluminium already broke through its moving averages in September, but had held above $3000/t until recently with the market still quite tight for now despite an expected 2027 surplus. Our expectations for the 2027 surplus haven't changed, driven new capacity in Indonesia and Angola, a recovery in West Asia and small smelter restarts in Europe and the US. Aluminium demand can also be particularly sensitive to an economic slowdown in the face of rising interest rates, while positioning on LME remains higher than the rest of the complex, implying potential for additional downside.
 
Zinc: from a fundamental perspective, we see a strong set up for zinc with a very tight supply side. Mine supply is expected to contract 1.8% in 2026 to 12.7 Mt, lower than output in 2015, while recovery next year is likely 2H weighted, leaving scope for further near-term tightness.  
ALSO READ: Chris Wood hikes exposure to Indian equities as AI trade falters
 
Meanwhile, ex-China remains reliant on Chinese exports to balance the market which face risks from domestic smelter struggles and falling SHFE inventories. However, demand has been weak, with less than 1% growth expected this year globally, while higher interest rates bring additional downside risk. LME zinc positioning looks unusual versus other metals, with both long and short positioning rising sharply,
highlighting diverging market views which could keep prices volatile.
 
Nickel: The market remains very focused on Indonesia's mining policy, particularly the upcoming release of RKAB (mining) quotas for 2027, which may remain restrictive. Some operators have also floated potential production cuts due to margin pressures with elevated energy and sulphur prices.
 
Disclaimer: Views and outlook in this report belong to the brokerages and analysts cited. They do not reflect the views of Business Standard. Readers are advised to exercise discretion.

data.title: Rupee could rise to 91.50/$ on equity inflows: HDFC Bank's treasury head
data.description:
The Indian rupee could gain to 91.50 against the US dollar if equity inflows remain strong and geopolitical risks stay in check, a top treasury official at the country's ​largest private bank said.

The Indian currency depreciated sharply till October, declining 8% against the ​US dollar at the lowest point of the year as foreign investors withdrew from equity markets in ‌Asia's third-largest economy due to high valuations and lack of AI investments.

Higher oil prices added to the pressure, prompting tough measures from the central bank, including a reserve requirement against large hedging transactions.

Markets turned in November, with global investors pumping a monthly record $12 billion into Indian equities.

 

"I believe 91.50 could be a possibility," said Arup Rakshit, group head for treasury at HDFC Bank in Mumbai in an interview late on Friday, adding that he sees the currency trading in a range of 91.50 to 93.50 in the near term.

On Friday, the rupee closed at 92.67 to the dollar.

The rupee has gained nearly 2.5% in November, turning sentiment in the offshore non-deliverable forwards market and prompting exporters to sell dollars, Rakshit said.

Additional dollar demand brought on by the Reserve Bank of ‌India's decision to impose a 20% foreign exchange risk reserve on large hedging transactions has also eased, he added.

"When the Reserve Bank of India introduced a foreign exchange risk reserve there was some additional dollar demand that came in from importers as absolute hedged import rates were lower, since the INR had immediately appreciated," Rakshit said.

"That demand is now reducing as the import cycle is typically 90 days and nearly half of that is over," he said, adding that importers are hedging less as the rupee strengthens and oil prices fall.

A 50 BASIS POINT HIKE?

While pressure on ​the currency has eased, inflation has breached the central bank's upper tolerance limit of 6%, prompting a few analysts to expect ‌a 50 basis point hike at its December meeting.

Rakshit does not rule this out.

"I think the repo rate will settle somewhere between 6.25-6.5%. A 25 basis point hike in December is more or less given. There ​is a section ‌of the market which is thinking it could be a 50 basis point hike and I would lean on that ‌side," he said.

Retail inflation rose to 6.09% in October and wholesale inflation rose to 12.3%.

Higher wholesale prices have yet to fully pass through into retail prices, Rakshit said, adding that food prices are also starting to rise.

This will ‌prompt ​the central bank ​to raise rates and keep liquidity tight at 0.6% to 1% of banking system deposits, he said.

Bond yields would also rise, but not sharply, he said.

"Immediately, I would put the top for the 10-year ‌at about 7.40% and ​then moving up to 7.50% to 7.60 levels max. I don't see it going beyond that," he said.

data.title: Like SpaceX, Anthropic ran an unusual IPO process, chafing some bankers
data.description:
For the second time this year, Wall Street bankers and lawyers took home a massive paycheck from a record-setting initial public offering. And for the second time this year, some of them came out of it complaining in private about how the process was riddled with complications and unlike any they had worked on before.
 
With SpaceX's IPO in June, in which banks earned half a billion dollars in fees, bankers chafed over how tightly the Elon Musk-led company controlled the months-long process and kept financial and other information private, making it hard for advisers to do their jobs.
 
As Anthropic's IPO, dubbed internally "Project Lantern", eclipsed SpaceX on Thursday and bankers took home more than half a billion dollars in fees, several people close to the process listed a litany of problems that had plagued the offering process: a compressed timeline, marred by last-minute changes and delays in sharing financial projections; rushed document approvals; and highly unusual restrictions on bankers and concern about leaks - especially after Reuters reported many details from a ‌draft IPO filing weeks before it was made public.
 
 
Anthropic, for example, instructed some of its 22 IPO underwriters to limit the number of ​bankers working on the deal to four, asking the firms to make sure they were senior staff, several people ​familiar with the matter said. One of the people said the restriction likely came out of fear that information would leak, and that the banks found a way to work around it anyway.
 
Underlying these complaints is a new power dynamic between technology companies and Wall Street. Companies ​such as SpaceX, Anthropic - and potentially also OpenAI in the future - have come to wield enormous power as the transformative potential of artificial intelligence creates a frenzied demand for their shares, and they are wielding it to do things their way. That is upsetting some bankers. But banks and investors appear to have little choice but to play along.
 
"These companies certainly did have some market power to tell underwriters that it's not going to be business as usual," said Jay Ritter, a University of Florida professor emeritus who researches IPOs. "But the big Wall Street firms, I suspect, are still going to be doing things as business as usual for all but maybe OpenAI (after these two deals)."
 
Ritter added that both SpaceX and Anthropic had negotiated to pay underwriters nothing on the additional shares sold through the greenshoe option. "I don't think most companies are going to be able to demand zero spread on ​overallotment shares," he said.
 
Anthropic, Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley, the two lead underwriters on the two IPOs, declined to comment.
 
SpaceX and OpenAI did not respond to requests for comment.
 
Both SpaceX and Anthropic debuted successfully, raising record amounts of money, and their shares rallied initially. A key part of the underwriters' job is to market the ‌securities. Thanks to the demand for AI, that was an easy sell - both companies had order books oversubscribed many times over.
 
After an initial burst in shares, the trajectories of the two big AI firms diverged. SpaceX climbed to a post-listing peak of $201.80 ​on June 16 before retreating below its $135 IPO price for the first time in mid-July. Anthropic's shares closed down 8.5% on Friday after a 17% first-day pop, as a dramatic unraveling of the AI trade showed that even a blockbuster listing could not shake the gloom hanging over the sector. 

UNUSUAL NON-COMPETES AND RESTRICTIONS

 
In the case of SpaceX's IPO, the people close to the process said Musk's team dictated terms at every stage. Musk's team told the largest and most powerful US banks - including Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley - how to market SpaceX's stock and to whom. It told some banks the specific order sizes they needed to "fill" - in some cases ‌a few billion dollars - and gave them instructions on what types of investors to bring. Banks signed on to underwrite ​the IPO without being told what they would be paid, the people said.
 
The underlying current running through Anthropic's IPO process was what ‌several of the people who spoke to Reuters interpreted as a sense of extreme caution.
 
Anthropic asked some senior officers at banks working on its IPO to sign legal documents restricting core members of the transaction team from working with rival companies, including OpenAI, Cursor, DeepSeek and ‌Hugging Face, for six months after it went public, according to the people.
 
Banks routinely manage conflicts and protect client confidentiality. But bankers and lawyers said it is rare for an IPO to impose exclusivity this broad, particularly on individual bankers.
 
In previous head-to-head IPOs such as those of ridesharing rivals Uber ​and Lyft, or real estate companies Trulia and Zillow, banks could simply pick a side, in part because the deals were smaller and required fewer banks.
 
Anthropic, by contrast, needed a broad syndicate to raise the enormous amount of capital it was seeking. That, some of the people said, explained why Anthropic sought to bind individual bankers with these restrictions.
 
One banker who declined to sign on to the agreement said it was a challenge to ​find people who could promise not to actively cover or engage with Anthropic's peers, especially as several of those companies pursue their own initial or secondary offerings. 

INFORMATION LEAKS AND LATE NIGHTS

 
Some of the restrictions were meant to control leaks of information.
 
Nearly four weeks before Anthropic's filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission, called Form S-1, was made public, Reuters reported on it, revealing details of the company's financials, risk factors, dealings with other tech companies and other information.
 
Anthropic also used a product called NetRoadshow ‌to share information, instead of regular PDFs, with most of the banks underwriting the deal.
 
NetRoadshow logs access details, including information such as who has seen the document and looked at which page. Documents on NetRoadshow also had individual bankers' names as watermarks.
 
Leaks continued to surface in the press, but using NetRoadshow ‌complicated bankers' work, including because the platform would not let them save copies of documents, one of the people said.
 
Anthropic planned to file an updated securities filing, called an S-1A, with the SEC with the price range and to launch the marketing on November 10. To do so, it needed to send a draft to all the banks in its syndicate for them to sign off on it.
 
The night before it was to happen, a law firm on the deal sent a PDF to the banks about the sale of shares in Canada. But soon it followed with another email asking them to disregard it, saying it "contains incorrect price range and share information," according to the email, which was seen by Reuters.
 
The correct S-1A was then sent via the NetRoadshow platform around 2 a.m. New York time. Banks were told they had several hours to sign off on it before it was filed with the ​SEC.

data.title: China opposes ban on Chinese telecoms' direct access to US phone numbers
data.description:
China firmly opposes ​the US Federal Communications Commission's vote to ban Chinese telecommunications firms from direct access to US phone numbers, ‌its commerce ​ministry said ​on Sunday.
 
Thursday's FCC ​decision, which cited national security concerns, will bar China Mobile, China Telecom and China ​Unicom and other IP-enabled service ‌providers from direct access.
 
The ​regulator has pushed for decoupling the US and China in ‌the telecoms, ​communications, and ‌testing and certification sectors, the ‌Chinese ministry said in a ​statement, adding the actions run counter to the consensus ​reached by the countries' leaders.
 
China urged ‌the United States to retract ‌the ban, warning it would take necessary counter measures.

data.title: Tata Steel to acquire 26.6% stake in APL Apollo for ₹15,510 crore
data.description:
Tata Steel on Monday announced a series of strategic transactions with APL Apollo Tubes, involving the sale of its steel tubes and colour-coated businesses, acquisition of a promoter stake in the company and a partnership to set up 5 million tonnes per annum (MTPA) of colour-coated steel manufacturing capacity across India.
 
The company will acquire a 26.6 per cent promoter stake in APL Apollo for about ₹15,510 crore and launch an open offer for a further 26 per cent.
 
In a statement, the company said it had executed agreements for a comprehensive strategic partnership covering the sale of its steel tubes and colour-coated businesses to APL Apollo, the acquisition of the entire promoter stake of 26.6 per cent in APL Apollo, and a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with SG Tech Engineering Private Ltd (SG Spectra), a company associated with the promoter group of APL Apollo, to set up exclusive contract manufacturing facilities of 5 MTPA of colour-coated products on a modular and pan-India basis to leverage growth in the Indian colour-coated products market.
 

Deal structure

On Sunday, Tata Steel executed agreements to sell all its shareholding in Tata Steel Colors Pvt Ltd, a wholly owned subsidiary, as well as its entire steel tubes business to APL Apollo Tubes Ltd.
 
This will consolidate Tata Steel’s surface-coated coil capacity of 800,000 tonnes per annum, as well as its 1.7 MTPA steel tubes business, in APL Apollo Pvt Ltd for a combined consideration of ₹28,000 crore.
 
APL Apollo will initially fund the acquisition through a mix of acquisition financing and subsequently replace the debt with long-term capitalisation to de-risk the balance sheet.
 
On Monday morning, Tata Steel executed agreements to acquire the 26.6 per cent promoter stake in APL Apollo Tubes Ltd at a price of ₹2,100 per share for a consideration of ₹15,510 crore.
 
Tata Steel will also make an open offer for an additional 26 per cent stake in APL Apollo Tubes Ltd at ₹2,301.40 per share for a consideration of ₹16,756 crore.
 
The transactions are subject to regulatory approvals, and Tata Steel expects to obtain these approvals in the coming months and close the composite set of transactions within FY27.

Downstream powerhouse

Tata Steel said that APL Apollo would now be the vehicle to drive downstream growth in steel tubes and colour-coated products. The new APL Apollo Tubes Pvt Ltd will build up to a 15.5 MTPA capacity by 2035, including 9 MTPA of steel tubes and 6.5 MTPA of colour-coated products.
 
The move is aimed at leveraging the combined strengths of the two companies, optimising capacity utilisation, unlocking value and improving profitability.
 
Commenting on the deal, T V Narendran, Chief Executive Officer (CEO) and Managing Director (MD) of Tata Steel, said: “We are very pleased to have entered into a comprehensive agreement with APL Apollo and the promoters as we create a downstream powerhouse for the future characterized by its inherent strengths of agility in the market, strong growth trajectory and benchmark capex-opex profile to serve the growing Indian market.”
 
This strategic move helps to consolidate the steel tubes and colour-coated businesses under Tata Steel’s ownership while unlocking multiple synergies between the two companies, he added. “This will create value for all stakeholders with enhanced customer centricity, pan-India reach, and a full product portfolio.”
 
Koushik Chatterjee, Executive Director (ED) and Chief Financial Officer (CFO) of Tata Steel, said: “We have over the last year emphasised our strategic intent to grow aggressively in the value-added space and expand our downstream footprint both organically and inorganically. While we have multiple projects under construction in value-added segments like tinplate and hot rolled pickled and galvanised lines, APL Apollo presented a unique opportunity for us.”
 
This is not just an acquisition of a very profitable and efficient company, but the best foundation to build a future business in the colour-coated space with an exclusive contract manufacturing agreement with SG Tech Engineering, an entity run by the promoters of APL Apollo, he said.
 
“Sanjay Gupta and his team have demonstrated experience in building downstream capacity with agility, speed and efficiency and this partnership will be very strategic for Tata Steel and APL Apollo in the future,” Chatterjee said, adding that APL Apollo not only adds growth from the first day with the transfer of Tata Steel’s business but also has the definite potential to be a very profitable 15.5 MTPA downstream company in the future.
